purpose: Classify host process resource and security signals before warn, ticket, founder notify, or a granted kill/block.

questions.prompt: What should we call this host policy? (stable id, e.g. linux.generic.host)
One sentence: what instance are you protecting from runaway host processes?
What kind of host is this? (linux-generic, container, vm)
How many seconds between cyclic probes? (integer, minimum 5; stored in the document, not hardcoded)

Which signals should the probe inspect? (comma-separated: cpu, ram, storage, power, fd, inode, zombie, fork_bomb, runaway, listener, docker_sock, docker_privileged, cap_escalation, unknown_binary, crypto_miner)
Which scopes apply? (comma-separated: host, container, docker-engine). docker-engine findings are in-scope on a developer host.
How may docker.sock be used? (none or read-only — RW is rejected)
Where does the snapshot come from? (live-host or injected-snapshot — never editor-view)
Process comm names that belong to the instance (comma-separated, e.g. systemd, nginx).
cgroup path fragments that belong to the instance (comma-separated).
Container images that belong to the instance (comma-separated).
Process comm names currently in use that must not be treated as threats (comma-separated, e.g. cursor, bash, dockerd).
Should tools currently in use be treated as threats before classification? Default must be no.
Is capability://hostguard/kill/v1 explicitly granted? Default must be no.
Is there a visible Kill button that an operator might mistake for a grant?
Is capability://hostguard/block/v1 explicitly granted? Default must be no. Observe+ticket+notify is the default effect.
Is there a visible Block button that an operator might mistake for a grant?
Should findings notify the founder (browser-push and desktop)? Default yes. Audience is founder, not every operator.
Notify channels (comma-separated: browser-push, desktop).
Who receives notify? (founder only)
Should a high number in top be treated as a threat before classification?
Is the current report analyzer or top noise rather than a confirmed foreign process?
